title: Agentic Data Engineering & Agentic Analytics Experience — video talking-point rubric
purpose: What a video covering MCG's agentic story is expected to say. gen-ceo-video-review.js classifies the actual narration against each criterion and reports what got missed.
note: Authored from the repo's own narrative sources, not invented. Every criterion carries a `source` pointing at the file that defines it. Edit this file to change what the review scores; the classifier binds to `id`, so keep ids stable.
sources: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md — two AI stories, six capabilities, seven-step flow, coding-agent loop, GA vs preview
cfg-agentic.json — outcomes row and the 30s/60s talk tracks
Meridian_Commerce_Group_Demo_Profile.md — company, CEO, the seven nightmares

scale.covered: Stated explicitly and clearly enough that a first-time viewer would take the point away.
scale.partial: Touched, implied, or named without enough substance to land — a viewer could miss it.
scale.missed: Not present in the narration at all.

weights.must: The video fails its job without this.
weights.should: Expected; its absence is a real gap worth fixing before the next cut.
weights.nice: Strengthens the story; acceptable to trade away for time.

dimensions.name: Agentic Data Engineering (build side)
dimensions.framing: The AI that helps author the pipeline and govern the data in the first place — one step upstream of the analytics. Build side produces trust; consumption side spends it.

criteria.name: Pipelines are code, in version control
criteria.expect: The pipeline is declarative YAML held in Git — reviewable, diffable, revertable — not something clicked together in a browser. CI/CD deploys the definition.

criteria.name: One definition, three ways to author it
criteria.expect: The same YAML file is editable visually in the Qlik Talend Cloud UI, programmatically in an IDE such as VS Code, or agentically by an AI coding agent — one schema, one Git history, whichever path the engineer takes.
criteria.source: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § Two AI stories; talking point 1

criteria.name: The agent types, the human decides
criteria.expect: A worked coding-agent loop: the agent edits the file, the schema validates the change live, the diff is small and reviewable, a human owns the decision, and a bad change is a git revert.
criteria.source: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § human-in-the-loop coding-agent loop; talking point 2

criteria.name: Data Product Agent
criteria.expect: Gold data products are packaged and reviewed conversationally — the two products being Supply Chain Health and Last Mile Performance, each with governance metadata and a trust-score SLA.

criteria.name: Data Quality Agent
criteria.expect: A steward states a rule in plain language — for example that every perishable item must carry a lot number — and the agent turns it into an enforced rule and shows the violations, feeding the trust scores on the silver datasets.

criteria.name: Catalog and Business Glossary Agent, with drafts held for approval
criteria.expect: Natural-language questions across the catalog, and generated glossary terms that arrive in draft status and wait for a human to approve them — the approval gate is the point, not a detail.

criteria.name: AI inside the pipeline task, not only on the dashboard
criteria.expect: Talend Agentic Routes put an LLM or RAG step inside a data task: a mangled multilingual address goes in, a structured corrected one with a confidence score comes back, above the threshold it continues automatically and below it goes to a human steward — and the model can run inside the customer's own tenant.

criteria.name: Qlik MCP Server exposes governance to any AI client
criteria.expect: The governed result — data products, quality metrics, lineage, catalog — is reachable by any MCP-compatible assistant, not locked inside one vendor's chat window.

criteria.name: Medallion on an open target
criteria.expect: Bronze through gold lands on the Qlik Open Lakehouse as Apache Iceberg tables on object storage — an open format, not a proprietary one.
criteria.source: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § Two AI stories; seven steps #2

criteria.name: Build side produces the trust the consumption side spends
criteria.expect: The explicit through-line between the two halves: the governed products this side builds are exactly what Answers, Predict and the Discovery Agent read. Without it the two halves look like separate products.
criteria.source: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § seven steps close; talking point 3

criteria.name: Honest about GA versus preview
criteria.expect: Declarative pipelines and the Qlik MCP Server are called out as preview, and the three conversational agents are described as Qlik Answers capabilities rather than separate products.
criteria.source: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § GA vs preview status; talking point 4

criteria.name: Anchored in Meridian's own numbers
criteria.expect: The engineering story is tied back to the business case — the $127M annual cost, the seven data nightmares, the four systems with no common key — rather than presented as generic capability.

dimensions.name: Agentic Analytics Experience (consumption side)
dimensions.framing: What people do with the trusted data: ask, watch, predict and act — with the governance visible rather than assumed.

criteria.name: Answers that cite their source
criteria.expect: A question over the operational document knowledge base returns an answer with the document attached — the NinjaVan contract amendment behind the Singapore delivery-accuracy fall is the worked example — so the viewer sees it did not guess.
criteria.source: series/s4_analytics/script.md scene 3; MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § Two AI stories

criteria.name: Dashboards authored conversationally over MCP
criteria.expect: Sheets and charts created by an assistant calling live Qlik tools against the real tenant, ending as governed objects in a governed app — plain English in, governed artifact out.

criteria.name: Prediction on the same governed data
criteria.expect: Qlik Predict trained on the governed lakehouse — cold-chain exceedance and late-delivery risk — with the insight that a missing tracking number is itself one of the strongest predictors, so the data gap predicts the failure.

criteria.name: Something is always watching the products
criteria.expect: A Discovery Agent monitors the gold products continuously against explicit thresholds — trust score, sync lag, volume shift — so the Rotterdam failure's seventy-two silent hours would now be an alert.

criteria.name: The loop closes without a person in it
criteria.expect: Automations carry detection through notification, review, correction and validation — a cold-chain breach posting to the operations channel, a steward's correction handed back to the pipeline — automated end to end except the step that should stay human.

criteria.name: The human gate is named on this side too
criteria.expect: Where a person approves, overrides or is escalated to — drafts awaiting approval, a steward queue, an override path — stated rather than implied, so the experience is not read as fully autonomous.
criteria.source: cfg-agentic.json analytics.aiml accent; MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § coding-agent loop

criteria.name: One governed product, many consumers
criteria.expect: Sheets, answers and predictions are shown reading the same two gold products, so the viewer sees one governed source rather than three disconnected AI features.

criteria.name: Tied to a decision someone actually makes
criteria.expect: At least one concrete operational decision that changes because of this — who acts, on what, how much sooner — rather than a tour of features.

criteria.name: Quantified outcome
criteria.expect: The business result carried in numbers the board already knows — against the $127M baseline and the accuracy, SLA and WISMO measures behind it.

criteria.name: Honest about what is live
criteria.expect: Consumption-side capabilities that are preview or forward-looking are labelled as such, consistent with how the build side is described.
